To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for ovulation induction medications for my patient. These medications are medically necessary for the treatment of anovulatory infertility and are supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) and the Endocrine Society.

CLINICAL SUMMARY

My patient has been diagnosed with [PCOS / hypothalamic anovulation / anovulatory infertility] (ICD-10 [E28.2 / N97.0]). She has failed [X] cycles of oral ovulation induction with [letrozole / clomiphene]. Injectable gonadotropins (follitropin alfa / menotropins) are the medically appropriate next step per ASRM guidelines.

DENIAL REBUTTAL

If denied as "not medically necessary": Anovulation is a diagnosable medical condition causing infertility. Ovulation induction is the medically necessary treatment. Without ovulation, pregnancy cannot occur. This is not an elective treatment.

If denied for "benefit exclusion": [If state mandate applies]: State law requires coverage of infertility treatment. Ovulation induction medications are a covered benefit under this mandate.

If denied for letrozole (off-label): Letrozole is the first-line treatment for PCOS per ASRM and the Endocrine Society (Legro et al., N Engl J Med. 2014;371:119-129). The fact that it is FDA-approved for a different indication does not make it experimental or inappropriate for this use. Off-label prescribing is standard medical practice.

EVIDENCE BASE

Legro RS, et al. (NEJM 2014) demonstrated that letrozole achieves higher live birth rates than clomiphene in PCOS (27.5% vs 19.1%). The ASRM Practice Committee and Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (2013) both recommend letrozole as first-line therapy for PCOS-related anovulation.

MONITORING NECESSITY

Serial transvaginal ultrasound monitoring (76830) during ovulation induction is medically necessary to prevent ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and reduce the risk of high-order multiple gestation. Denial of monitoring ultrasounds creates a patient safety risk.

CONCLUSION

I respectfully request reconsideration and approval of ovulation induction medications and monitoring for my patient.

Sincerely,
{{physician_name}}, {{credentials}}
